land.text: the Tihamah coastal strip, about 80 mi long and 40 mi inland around Sabya and Jizan, where Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi 'began to establish political control' about 1906; the Ottomans had held Asir since 1871 and set up a sub-governorate at Abha in 1872 under the Yemen vilayet

predecessors.note: Emirate page: 'existed from 1907'; Muhammad proclaimed himself Imam on 24 December 1908.

land.text: Abha and the highlands (taken 1920) and, by 1923, 'the rest of Asir' in the Tihamah; the Saudis' Emirate of Nejd row

successors.note: Emirate page: protectorate 20 November 1930, formally annexed 1934 (Treaty of Taif); the Saudi-Yemeni war (1934) page: the Emir of Asir 'assented to Saudi suzerainty' in 1926 and the emirate was incorporated in 1930 (ledger: vassal_start 1926, vassal_end and dissolve November 1930). The Abha highlands went to the emirate-of-nejd entry in 1920.

land.text: Abha and the highlands, taken in 1920 and divided with al-Idrisi's Tihamah tribes in the fall of 1920

successors.note: Cliopatria's Emirate of Nejd row ends in 1925.

land.text: Hodeidah (and Al Luhayyah): the Hodeidah page has 'Yemen captured the city in April 1925'; the Mutawakkilite page has Imam Yahya capturing it after Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi's death ('after 1923')

successors.note: April 1925 (Hodeidah page); the Al Luhayyah part is a confidence-1 bridge to the same year.

capitals.name: Sabya
capitals.note: Emirate page: 'Its capital was Sabya.' Coordinates are the researcher's (Sabya is not in the gazetteer). Abha, the Ottoman and later Saudi regional seat, was Al Aid's and then Ibn Saud's.

correction.text: the Tihamah coastal strip, about 80 mi long and 40 mi inland (Jizan and Sabya), as the lowland part of Cliopatria's later Asir shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Asir row begins in 1917 but the Emirate page has it 'from 1907' (Muhammad proclaimed himself Imam on 24 December 1908; the Asir Province page: 'about 1906'). Its first land is the Tihamah coastal strip, about 80 mi long and 40 mi inland, so the Cliopatria shape's lowland part is used (57 cells, about 14 k km2, against about 8 k km2 from the page's 80 by 40 miles; ratio 1.7). Al Luhayyah and Az Zaydiyah (autumn 1909) are in the next keyframe, the Farasan Islands (1915) in asir_1915.

correction.text: the Tihamah strip with Al Luhayyah and Az Zaydiyah, taken in autumn 1909 (the radii are the researcher's readings; neither town is in the gazetteer)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Az Zaydiyah and Al Luhayyah were taken in autumn 1909' (Emirate page). The treaty of al-Hafa'ir (ratified January 1910) made al-Idrisi Kaymakam of Asir and fighting resumed in October 1910 at Abha, Al Luhayyah and Midi; the page does not say who held the towns afterwards, so they are kept for 1909-1910 and dropped with a confidence-1 loss in 1911 (the Province page: 'The Idrisis were defeated in 1911 by Hashemites forces under Hussein bin Ali'). Added after review: the 1909 gain had no matching loss and the towns were in no keyframe.

correction.text: the Tihamah coastal strip, about 80 mi long and 40 mi inland (Jizan and Sabya), as the lowland part of Cliopatria's later Asir shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Tihamah strip again after the 1911 defeat by the Hashemite forces under Hussein bin Ali (Province page); same shape as asir_1907 (about 14 k km2 against 8 k km2 from the page's 80 by 40 miles).

correction.text: the Tihamah strip with the Farasan Islands, captured from the Ottomans in 1915

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1915, the Idrisids had captured the oil-rich Farasan Islands archipelago from the Ottomans' (Emirate page); the ledger's 1915 gain had no keyframe before 1917.

correction.text: the Tihamah coast with the Farasan Islands only, for 1917-1918: Cliopatria's lowland cells without the Abha highlands, which enter in 1919

keyframe_review.note: Corrected after review: Cliopatria's 95.6 k km2 shape (the Asir province, Jizan and a piece of Makkah province, no Najran and no Yemen) is the emirate as it stood after the war, not in 1917-1918. The Province page: 'After the end of World War I, Muhammad ibn Ali became ruler of an internationally recognized sovereign state ... until he died in 1920. The territories of the emirate reached from Abha in the north to Hodeidah in the south', so the highlands come with the 1919 gain from the Ottoman Empire (ledger; the ottoman-empire dossier's 1919 loss of Asir mirrors it), and 1917-1918 keeps the Tihamah strip (57 cells, about 14 k km2) and the Farasan Islands (1915). The Province page says the Saudis took Abha in 1920 and has no infobox area for the emirate (76,693 km2 is the modern Saudi province, ratio 1.25 to the Cliopatria shape); the Emirate page gives 'an 80 mi long strip of the Tihamah region' about 40 mi inland (about 8 k km2).

correction.text: the 1917 shape with the Farasan Islands and Al Luhayyah, 'handed over to the Emirate of Asir' in 1919

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: in 1919 the British handed Al Luhayyah 'over to the Emirate of Asir' under the Anglo-Idrisi treaty, which extends the Tihamah south of Cliopatria's 16.4 N limit. Al Luhayyah is not in the gazetteer (a 40 km radius at 42.7 E 15.7 N is used). The highlands are in this shape because of the 1919 gain from the Ottoman Empire (ledger), which the Province page places after the end of the war and before the Saudi capture of Abha in 1920.

correction.text: the Tihamah: Ibn Saud got the Qahtan, Shahran, Wadi'a and Rufayda mountain tribes and al-Idrisi the Tihamah tribes

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Saudi troops took Abha about April-May 1920 (Province page: 'The Saudis took control of the regional capital Abha in 1920') and the fall-1920 Saudi-Idrisi treaty divided the tribes, the highland ones to Ibn Saud and the Tihamah ones to al-Idrisi. The shape keeps only the Tihamah part of Cliopatria's shape (57 cells) with the islands and Al Luhayyah; Cliopatria keeps the highlands to 1923.

correction.text: the Tihamah from Jizan to Hodeidah, the widest extent of the emirate in 1921

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'in 1921, they handed over Hodeidah' and 'by handing over Hodeidah to the Idrisids, the state had reached its widest borders' (Emirate page; the subject of 'they' is not clear in the extract and is read as the British, who handed Al Luhayyah over in 1919). The Tihamah from Jizan to Hodeidah is far smaller than Cliopatria's 95.6 k km2 (82 cells, about 21 k km2). Hodeidah was taken over when 'Britain evacuated the city on 29 January 1921, allowing it to be taken by the Emirate of Asir' (Hodeidah page).

correction.text: the Tihamah from Jizan to Hodeidah in 1922-1923

keyframe_review.note: 95.6 k km2 in Cliopatria, identical to 1917: the highlands the Saudis took in 1920 are still inside. The Province page has the Saudis 'incorporated the rest of Asir by 1923' (read as the highland Asir, since the Emirate page keeps the Tihamah emirate to 1930); Cliopatria's shape is therefore replaced by the 1921 Tihamah for 1922-1924. Hodeidah is kept to 1924 because the Hodeidah page has 'Yemen captured the city in April 1925' (it was 1924 in the first version, from the Mutawakkilite page's 'after 1923'); the war against Imam Yahya over Hodeidah (1919-1925) is in the ledger.

correction.text: the Idrisid remnant on the Tihamah coast around Jizan and Sabya, with the Farasan Islands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row ends in 1923 but the Emirate page keeps the emirate to the protectorate of 20 November 1930 (the Saudi-Yemeni war (1934) page: in 1926 it assented to Saudi suzerainty, and in 1930 it was incorporated into the Nejd and Hejaz Kingdom). Yemen captured Hodeidah in April 1925 (Hodeidah page), so the remnant is the Jizan-Sabya Tihamah and the Farasan Islands; Al Luhayyah is taken out in the same year (confidence 1; the war page has the Saudis taking it from Yemen on 1 May 1934). No page gives the extent of the remnant, which is the Cliopatria shape's own lowland part (the war page: 'Asir and Jizan were both part of the Idrisid Asir emirate during the 1920s' and the territory 'fluctuated').

region.text: the Tihamah coastal strip, about 80 mi long and 40 mi inland, capital Sabya

ledger.note: 1907: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi's emirate begins on the Tihamah coast. Emirate page: 'existed from 1907'; he proclaimed himself Imam on 24 December 1908, and the Asir Province page has him beginning 'to establish political control of Asir' 'in about 1906'. The page gives a strip, not a frontier.

region.text: Al Luhayyah and Az Zaydiyah (neither is in the gazetteer; the radii are approximate readings)

ledger.note: 1909: the Idrisi take Az Zaydiyah and Al Luhayyah. 'Az Zaydiyah and Al Luhayyah were taken in autumn 1909.' The page does not say how long they were kept; in 1910 Abha, Al Luhayyah and Midi were fought over and Al Luhayyah came back to the emirate only in 1919. Added after review: the towns are in asir_1909 and are dropped again by the confidence-1 loss of 1911.

region.text: Al Luhayyah and Az Zaydiyah (neither is in the gazetteer; the radii are approximate readings)

ledger.note: 1911: the Idrisi lose the two towns. The Province page: 'The Idrisis were defeated in 1911 by Hashemites forces under Hussein bin Ali' (then loyal to the Ottomans); the Emirate page has fighting at Abha, Al Luhayyah and Midi from October 1910 and the British handing Al Luhayyah over in 1919, and says nothing in between, so the year and the holder are a bridge.
1915: the Farasan Islands are captured. The page dates the capture to 1915, the year of the secret alliance with Britain (a 'Treaty of Friendship and Goodwill' of April 1915).
1919: Britain hands Al Luhayyah to Asir. 'The British handed Al Luhayyah over to the Emirate of Asir' under the Anglo-Idrisi treaty.

region.text: Abha and the highlands of Cliopatria's Asir shape outside the Tihamah

ledger.note: 1919: the emirate's territory reaches Abha. 'After the end of World War I, Muhammad ibn Ali became ruler of an internationally recognized sovereign state ... until he died in 1920. The territories of the emirate reached from Abha in the north to Hodeidah in the south'; the Saudis took Abha in 1920. The page gives no year for the gain, so 1919 is the year between the end of the war and the Saudi capture; the ottoman-empire dossier has the matching 1919 loss of Asir (confidence 1).

region.text: Hodeidah, claimed by the Imam as part of Yemen

ledger.note: 1919: war with Imam Yahya begins over the Tihamah to Hodeidah. Intermittent warfare with Imam Yahya in 1919-1923; the Imam considered al-Hudaydah 'to be a part of Yemen'. The page gives the span, not a first campaign.

region.text: Abha and the highland tribes (Qahtan, Shahran, Wadi'a, Rufayda), the part of Cliopatria's shape outside the Tihamah

ledger.note: 1920: the Saudis take Abha and the highlands. 'The Saudis took control of the regional capital Abha in 1920'; around April-May 1920 Saudi troops 'took down' Hasan ibn A'id near Abha, and in the fall of 1920 a Saudi-Idrisi treaty divided the tribes, the mountain ones to Ibn Saud and the Tihamah ones to al-Idrisi (Emirate page). The page gives tribes, so the highland region is the researcher's reading.

29 January 1921: Hodeidah passes to the Emirate. 'Britain evacuated the city on 29 January 1921, allowing it to be taken by the Emirate of Asir' (Hodeidah page; Britain had occupied it in January 1919); the Emirate page: 'In 1921, they handed over Hodeidah' and 'by handing over Hodeidah to the Idrisids, the state had reached its widest borders'.

1925: Al Luhayyah passes to Yemen with Hodeidah. No page dates it; it is bridged to the capture of Hodeidah because the Saudi-Yemeni war (1934) page has the Saudis taking Al Luhayyah from Yemen on 1 May 1934.

April 1925: Yemen captures Hodeidah. 'Yemen captured the city in April 1925' (Hodeidah page; a British report of 25 March 1925 had described a Yemeni offensive against Asir). The Mutawakkilite page has Imam Yahya capturing it 'after 1923', after the death of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi; the first version of this dossier bridged that to 1924.

April 1925: the war with Imam Yahya over Hodeidah ends with his capture of the town ('Yemen captured the city in April 1925', Hodeidah page), after the Emirate page's span of intermittent warfare in 1919-1923.

region.text: the Idrisid remnant on the Tihamah coast around Jizan and Sabya, with the Farasan Islands

ledger.note: 1926: the Emir of Asir accepts Saudi suzerainty. 'In 1926, the Emir of Asir assented to Saudi suzerainty, and in 1930 it was incorporated into the Nejd and Hejaz Kingdom' (Saudi-Yemeni war (1934) page; the Emirate page speaks of the protectorate treaty of Ibn Saud and Hassan al-Idrisi without a date). As the vassal's own side of the event the counterpart names the suzerain; the Saudi dossier would carry the same event with this state as counterpart. The Hejaz and Nejd row of Cliopatria (1926-1935) probably already covers this land.

20 November 1930: the suzerainty ends in incorporation. 'On 20 November 1930, the territory was incorporated as a protectorate of the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd' (Emirate page; formal annexation 1934 under the Treaty of Taif); the incorporation is the dissolve that follows.

region.text: the Idrisid Tihamah remnant around Jizan and Sabya

ledger.note: 20 November 1930: the Idrisid emirate is absorbed by the Saudis. Emirate page: 'the territory was incorporated as a protectorate' of the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd on 20 November 1930 (formally annexed in 1934, Treaty of Taif). The Saudi-Yemeni war page has Asir accepting Saudi suzerainty in 1926 and being incorporated in 1930; the Province page has the Saudis incorporating 'the rest of Asir by 1923', read here as the highlands.

wars.name: Idrisi-Ottoman fighting for Asir
wars.outcome: The Idrisi took Az Zaydiyah and Al Luhayyah in autumn 1909, made peace at al-Hafa'ir (ratified January 1910, al-Idrisi becoming Kaymakam of Asir) and fought again from October 1910; in 1915 al-Idrisi allied with Britain and took the Farasan Islands.
wars.note: The page does not say who held Al Luhayyah after 1910. The Asir Province page has the Idrisi defeated in 1911 by Hashemite forces under Hussein, then loyal to the Ottomans; Qunfudhah was contested with the Sharif of Mecca. The ledger drops the two towns in 1911 (bridge) on the Province page's 'defeated in 1911'.

wars.name: Idrisi-Yemeni conflict over Hodeidah
wars.outcome: Intermittent warfare with Imam Yahya, who considered Hodeidah part of Yemen; the Idrisids received Hodeidah on 29 January 1921 when Britain evacuated it, and Yemen captured it in April 1925 (Hodeidah page; the Mutawakkilite page: after the death of Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi, 'after 1923').
wars.note: Cliopatria's North Yemen row begins in 1919 and touches Asir 1919-1923. The first version of this dossier ended the war in 1924; the Hodeidah page gives April 1925.

wars.name: Saudi conquest of Asir
wars.outcome: The Saudis took Abha in 1920, divided the tribes with al-Idrisi in the fall of 1920 and 'incorporated the rest of Asir by 1923' (the highlands; the Tihamah emirate lasted to 1930).
wars.note: Ibn Saud sent Ikhwan warriors; Hasan Al Idrissi left for Yemen under Imam Yahya's protection (no date). The Saudi-Yemeni war of 1934 and the Treaty of Taif are later and outside the Cliopatria row.

certainty.note: Tribal and coastal frontiers; no page opened gives a treaty line (the fall-1920 Saudi-Idrisi treaty divides tribes, not a boundary).

notes: REPAIRED after review. Pages opened: Asir Province, Idrisid Emirate of Asir, Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen (for north-yemen), and now Hodeidah and Saudi-Yemeni war (1934), against a budget of 1-2; the last two were opened to settle the review's findings on the Saudi suzerainty and on the date Hodeidah was lost. The Hasan al-Idrisi page the reviewer named returned url_not_found, so the extent of the remnant in 1925-1930 is still unknown. Changes: (1) asir_1917 is now only the Tihamah strip with the Farasan Islands for 1917-1918, and the highlands enter through a 1919 gain from the Ottoman Empire (Province page: after the war the emirate 'reached from Abha in the north to Hodeidah in the south'; the Saudis took Abha in 1920; the ottoman-empire dossier's 1919 loss of Asir mirrors it); (2) the 1909 gain of Al Luhayyah and Az Zaydiyah is in a new keyframe asir_1909 and is closed by a confidence-1 loss in 1911 (the Province page's defeat by Hussein bin Ali; no page says who held the towns before Britain handed Al Luhayyah over in 1919), and the Farasan Islands (1915) now have their own keyframe asir_1915; (3) vassal_start 1926 (Emir of Asir assents to Saudi suzerainty, Saudi-Yemeni war page) and vassal_end 20 November 1930 with the Hejaz and Nejd kingdom as counterpart; (4) Hodeidah: the Hodeidah page has Britain evacuating it on 29 January 1921 for the Emirate and Yemen capturing it in April 1925, so the loss moved from 1924 (confidence 1) to April 1925 (confidence 3) and keyframe asir_1924 became asir_1925. The north-yemen dossier (another verdict, not touched here) still has its mirror gain in 1924 and should read April 1925. Life 1907-20 November 1930, longer than Cliopatria's 1917-1923 (Emirate page 'existed from 1907'; protectorate 1930, annexed 1934). Cliopatria's single Asir shape (1917-1923, 95.6 k km2) is the Asir province plus Jizan and a piece of Makkah province, no Najran and nothing south of 16.4 N; it is used for the highlands from 1919 to 1920 and for the Tihamah cells throughout. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd row (1926-1935) probably still covers the remnant: treat it as a vassal of the Saudis from 1926. Not settled: who held Abha before the war's end (the Province page as first read had Hasan ibn Ali Al Aid 'virtually independent' there; the second reading does not mention him); where the 1910-1915 front stood; when Al Luhayyah passed from the Idrisids to Yahya (bridged to April 1925); the extent of the remnant in 1925-1930; the end of Muhammad ibn Ali's reign (died 1920 in the Province page's text, 1923 in the Emirate page's biography line) and Hasan al-Idrisi's succession (the Emirate page's infobox lists ruler periods 1906-1923, 1923-1926 and 1926-1934 without labels). The Treaty of al-Hafa'ir (January 1910, al-Idrisi as Ottoman Kaymakam) is a vassal event for the Ottoman dossier; the British treaty of April 1915 is not a vassalage on any page. Counterparts: emirate-of-nejd and kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd (me-10; the Hejaz and Nejd dossier does not exist yet), north-yemen (this group), kingdom-of-great-britain (eu-11; Al Luhayyah 1919, Hodeidah 1921), ottoman-empire (me-10). Gazetteer names needed: Al Luhayyah, Az Zaydiyah, Sabya, Farasan Islands (radii at approximate coordinates are used). Wikidata Q15728206 is the Asir Province article's id.
